title: I vibed a polished action arcade music game in 1 month for Cursor Vibe Jam
author: pohling2
selftext:
Link to play in browser: [https://beatbackgame.com/?ref=vibejam](https://beatbackgame.com/?ref=vibejam)

I spent about 120 hours on this project starting early April. I used Cursor and Claude with a stack of pure Typescript + Canvas 2D. Everything from the visuals to music is generated with pure code. Mobile works too, but desktop is recommended cause playing from you're phone browser isn't optimal (definitely doable if you're used to mobile D-Pads)

My biggest tip is start with a small scope and don't get started with an established engine - build an engine with AI that can do what you value in your game and support the platforms you need. Carefully plan this process with AI and always keep performance in mind. Your iteration loop for testing and debugging features needs to be smooth. If you hit a wall don't give up, just try another approach.

  
At the end of the day, you are the designer and must make meaningful decisions to align your vision with what you're making. Good thing AI is a good creative collaborator as well.

  
There is much I want to add to the game -the survivors-like upgrade system is almost ready. The 3 challenges I have up now I feel are pretty polished so I want to see many new names on the leaderboards!

  
Happy to answer any questions. I hope to share my other AI games here which I've spent 3-6 months on.

  
\*Also - please someone beat my score! Send me a DM about your playing experience or how the game can improve.

comments.author: darknessinducedlove
comments.body:
No offense but im tired of most of the projects I see here lacking any sort of imagination or artistry. Its always the same rushed looking nonsense.

Its entirely possible to create a really unseen experience within this time frame, but so many of these projects I see are just.. meh
